title: Grass-silage hydrothermal conditioning, washing, and pressing test conditions (abstract-level extract)
description: Traceable extract of the experimental condition levels and qualitative findings explicitly reported in the accessible abstract and conclusion for King et al. (2012). No numerical press-juice yield, cake composition, or treatment effect sizes were inferred.
source_title: The effects of hydrothermal conditioning, detergent and mechanical pressing on the isolation of the fibre-rich press-cake fraction from a range of grass silages
authors: C. King; J. McEniry; P. O'Kiely; M. Richardson
geography: Experimental grass grown at Teagasc Grange, Ireland
source_location: Accessible publisher abstract and conclusion; journal pages 179-188. Detailed article tables were not accessible during this extraction.
license: No open reuse license was identified in the accessible publisher record; retain citation and confirm rights before redistribution of article content.
applicability: Direct experimental protocol evidence for grass silage, including perennial ryegrass, cocksfoot, Italian ryegrass, and timothy. It is not fresh roadside-grass evidence and is not a validated operating point for the GreenHub press.
conversion_and_scaling: Reported test levels and qualitative conclusions are transcribed from the abstract/conclusion. The 3:1 water-to-silage notation is preserved without interpreting its mass/volume basis. No scaling or performance equation was derived.
uncertainty: Abstract-level reporting only. Numerical response tables, replicate uncertainty, detailed feed composition, and full protocol context were not available for this extraction.
provenance_note: This evidence expands the Phase 3 literature pool only. It does not change defaults, activate a route, or qualify as D4 calculation-connected evidence.
